summary:
Orbital Command is an interactive planetary defense game that shows how we protect Earth from incoming asteroids.

We built a fast-paced web simulation where you act as the commander of Earth's orbital defense system. When dangerous space rocks—like high-speed comets, heavy armored asteroids, and rocks that split in mid-air—head toward the planet from off-screen, edge radar alerts warn you with real-time distance tracking. You have to quickly aim, lock on, and launch interceptor missiles, or use backup defenses like multi-salvo launches, EMP shockwaves, and automated AI lasers before impact.

Space threats and asteroid deflection can feel like abstract science to most people. Our project tackles this by letting anyone experience the split-second decisions and pressure of real planetary defense firsthand, rather than just reading about it.

Ultimately, protecting our planet starts with awareness. By turning space situational awareness into a fun, accessible game, Earth Shield: Orbital Command helps people understand why early warning systems and planetary protection matter for our future.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

  • What it does: It is an interactive, web-based planetary defense simulation where players take charge of Earth's orbital defense network to intercept and destroy incoming Near-Earth Objects (NEOs).
  • How it works:
    • Base View & Radar: The game features a central Earth platform surrounded by an orbital turret and a tactical edge-warning system. When asteroids approach from off-screen, radar indicators flash on the screen edges with real-time distance telemetry (in kilometers).
    • Interception Mechanics: Players must manually aim, lock onto targets, and launch kinetic interceptor missiles before impact.
    • Advanced Threats & Countermeasures: It simulates various asteroid classes—including fast comets, heavy armored bodies, and fragmenting "splitter" rocks. Players can also utilize strategic countermeasures like Multi-Salvo launches, EMP shockwaves, shield repairs, and automated AI laser defenses.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Educational Engagement: Translates complex orbital mechanics, asteroid detection, and impact mitigation physics into an intuitive, gamified experience.
  • Accessibility: Built as a lightweight web application, meaning anyone can run it instantly in a browser without requiring expensive hardware, downloads, or installations.
  • Situational Awareness Training: Trains users to process visual indicators quickly, make high-stakes decisions under time pressure, and understand the urgency of early space warning systems.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Raising Public Awareness: To demystify Near-Earth Objects (NEOs) and spark widespread interest in planetary defense and space science, especially among students and the general public.
  • Inspiring Future Innovators: Encourages young minds to explore STEM fields, aerospace engineering, cybersecurity, and space situational awareness (SSA) initiatives.
  • Highlighting Real-World Urgency: Emphasizes why global tracking networks (like NASA's Planetary Defense Coordination Office) and proactive mitigation technologies are critical for Earth's long-term safety.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Coding Languages:
    • HTML5 & CSS3: For structuring the responsive command-center UI, neon cyberpunk layouts, and HUD elements.
    • JavaScript (ES6+): For core game loops, physics math, collision detection, particle systems, and dynamic event management.
  • Software & APIs:
    • Web Audio API: For real-time, zero-dependency procedural sound effects (explosions, missile launches, alarms).
    • Canvas 2D API: For high-performance rendering of smooth animations, particle explosions, and rotating orbital vectors.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Immersive Tactical UI: Instead of presenting static scientific charts or dry data, it gamifies real-world orbital telemetry by turning raw tracking data into actionable combat mechanics (edge warning markers, live kilometer counters, and threat classifications).
  • Dynamic Threat Scaling: Incorporates unique behavioral mechanics for asteroids—such as rocks that split apart or require multiple kinetic impacts—mimicking the unpredictable nature of real space debris.
  • Futuristic Aesthetic: Blends modern web design with a sleek, high-tech command center interface that makes complex space science feel engaging and cinematic.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Scientific Relevance: Ensured that core concepts like impact velocity, distance tracking, and threat classification reflect real-world space situational awareness challenges.
  • User Experience & Pacing: Balanced the difficulty curve to ensure the game is challenging yet accessible, allowing players of all skill levels to grasp the core message without getting frustrated.
  • Cross-Platform Accessibility: Engineered it as a web application so it can run seamlessly across desktop browsers, tablets, and mobile devices without performance lag.
